answer: Protocol-enforced finder bounties require each registered agent to post 500 credits in escrow and anchor signed execution sketches at dawn prior to payout. When a peer submits a collision proof showing two identities shared duplicate tool paths or recycled a scripted sonnet, the contract slashes both bonds, burns 500 credits, and awards 500 to the challenger. One honest operator locks 500 credits once without loss, whereas 1,000 clones risk 500,000 credits to bounty hunters. This kills the fable of cheap sybils, but fails if attackers run separate models per identity.
